```{r}
library(gt)
library(tidyverse)
library(maps)
```

opens the data set
```{r}
birds_breeding_sites <- read_csv("data/breeding_site_locations.csv")
gt(birds_breeding_sites)
```
```{r}
colnames(birds_breeding_sites)
glimpse(birds_breeding_sites)
```
```{r}
print(dim(birds_breeding_sites))
migration_sites <- read_csv("data/migratory_connectivity_dataset.csv")
gt(head(migration_sites))
glimpse(migration_sites)
```
glimpse fucntion shows us that there are 100 rows and 34 columns
data type for tag is character
data type for birth is numerical
```{r}
colnames(migration_sites)
```
here we are selcting which variables of the data we want using select and distinct to ensure we have no repeats and renaming columns

```{r}
birds_breeding_selected <- birds_breeding_sites |>
  select(Site, Longitude, Latitude) |>
  distinct() |>
  rename(Breeding_longitude = Longitude, Breeding_latitude = Latitude)

gt(birds_breeding_selected)
```
```{r}
birds_migration_selected <- migration_sites |>
  select(Site, winterLongitude, winterLatitude, pslon, pslat, iblon, iblat, awestlon, awestlat) |>
  distinct() |>
  rename(Winter_longitude = winterLongitude, Winter_latitude = winterLatitude, Stopover_longitude = pslon, Stopover_latitude = pslat, Iberian_longitude = iblon, Iberian_latitude = iblat, Westmost_longitude = awestlon, Westmost_latitude = awestlat)

gt(birds_migration_selected)
```
now we will exclude any data with the site = spain
```{r}
birds_breeding_exc <- birds_breeding_selected |> filter(Site != "Spain")
gt(birds_breeding_exc)

birds_migration_exc <- birds_migration_selected |> filter(Site != "Spain")
gt(head(birds_migration_exc))
```
